The petitioner has filed the present claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- along with interest, for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 14.02.2024..
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 14.02.2024 at about 2.00 p.m., the petitioner was returning to home from his college on his bicycle near M.N. Krishna Rao park, on BP Wadiyar road,
Basavanagudi, SCCH-10 Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-50-B-4249 came with with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's bicycle.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to hospital and took inpatient treatment.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
The respondent No.1 being insurer and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present petition.
3. In pursuance to the Petition notice, the respondent No.1(insurance company) has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Despite service of notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
SCCH-10 4.
The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 (insurer) are as under:

sentences.text:
The respondent No.1 being insurer of offending vehicle has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-B-4249, however the liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further, the respondent No.1 has denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and its involvement in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, the petitioner has filed the false case against the offending vehicle for wrongful loss to this respondent.

Further, the respondent No.1 has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries,
medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and SCCH-10 exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.1 prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 14.02.2024 at about 2.00 p.m., while he was proceeding on his bicycle and when he reached near Krishnarao Park, B.P. Odeyar Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B-4249 driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, as a result of the same, he fell down and sustained injuries ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
6.

The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW-2 and also examined H.R. Manager of New India Assurance company as PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to SCCH-10 Ex.P.28.
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :

ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 14.02.2024.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR in crime No.0020/2024 of Basavanagudi Traffic PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Maruthi Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg. No. KA-50-B-4249 for the commission of offences punishable u/s SCCH-10 279 and 337of IPC.
Ex.P3 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Basavanagudi Traffic PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.3, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Arun. K. S, who is none other than the driver of the offending Car for the offence punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
10.

Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.10 produced by petitioner and discharge summary i.e.
Ex.P.11, it appear that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

11. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle was SCCH-10 driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
12. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a Motor Vehicles Accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view is supported by the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: 13. Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Maruti Suzuki Swift Car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-B-4249.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE No.2:-

The petitioner contended that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Basavanagudi Medical Center SCCH-10 hospital, wherein he took inpatient treatment and spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.

Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
Future Medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.10.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
16. In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P.11.

On perusal of Ex.P.11 discharge summary of Basavanagudi Medical Center, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the said hospital SCCH-10 on 14.02.2024 and discharged on 17.02.2024 and it also discloses that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bone of forearm M/3 right side.
17.
Ex.P.12 are the medical bills and Ex.P.14 are the prescriptions.

During the cross-examination,
PW-1 has deposed that, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- was received by him from Medi Claim.

PW-3 H.R.
Manager of New India Assurance company has deposed that, the petitioner has obtained Group Medi Claim policy and a claim amount of Rs.1,00,000/- was paid to the petitioner.
According to him, out of Rs.2,00,000/- they have reimbursed a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as he has paid the insurance premium towards medi claim.
But no documents are produced in this regard.
The learned counsel for the petitioner by relying on the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Bombay in 2025 0 Supreme (Bom) 473 has submitted that,

sentences.text: under Medi Claim policy or under a Medical Insurance policy, is not liable to be SCCH-10 deducted from the amount of compensation payable to a claimant under the head Medical expenses in proceedings under Sec.166 of M.V. Act.
In the instant case, the petitioner has produced 10 medical bills out of which Sl No.2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 are only the original medical bills which amounting to Rs.12,171/-.
Further, no documents are produced to show that he has received only part amount from his Medi Claim policy.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for the amount of original medical bills of Rs.12,171/- only and same is rounded off to Rs.12,200/-
under the head of Medical expenses.
18.
As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards SCCH-10 nourishment and diet food it would be just.
19. The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury he has undergone surgery and suffering from permanent disability.
He has further stated that, due to the disability he has lost his earning capacity.

In order to establish the disability, the doctor was examined before the Court as PW- 2. PW-2 during his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained fracture middle third of both bones of right forearm and conducted surgery by closed reduction and intra medullary tens nail under general anesthesia and under C arm monitor.

Further deposed that, recently for assessment of disability, he examined the petitioner on 24.06.2025 and recent x-ray shows tens nail in situ and union of fracture and the petitioner has suffered physical impairment disability of 62.8%
to right upper limb and 21% to the whole body.
Though PW-2 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
SCCH-10 20

. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 21 years at the time of accident and he was doing 7th semester pharmacy at VV Puram college and also he was conducting tuition classes to class 5th to 10th standard and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.

At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4)
KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the SCCH-10 absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner would be just and proper.
The accident was occurred on 14.02.2024.

Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,500/- as monthly Vivek Narayan Singh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173834261/

21. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
22. As per the doctor, the body disability is approximately 21%.
It is settled principles of law that all permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 21% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the SCCH-10 nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 15%.
23.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.15.

As per Ex.P.15,
the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 03.01.2003.
The accident was occurred on 14.02.2024.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 21 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable for his age is 18.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 15%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,98,000/-(Rs.16,500 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,98,000/-(annual income) X 18 (multiplier) X 15% = Rs.5,34,600/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.5,34,600/-.
24.
The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries SCCH-10 suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.40,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.

25. PW-2 doctor has deposed in his examination chief that, second surgery is necessary for implant removal and approximate cost for hospitalization would be around Rs.1,50,000/- and the petitioner requires rest for three weeks.
Further, x-ray shows fracture united with implant in situ.
On perusal of recent x-ray produced by PW-2, it reveals that the implants are in situ.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards under the head of Future Medical expenses it would be just.
The future medical expenses does not carry any interest.

26. Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;

6) Future Medical expenses Rs. 50,000 /-
 Total Rs.7,01,800/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,01,800/-.
27. REGARDING LIABILITY:

As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-50-B-4249.
In this case, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.1, as such, respondent No.1 has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, SCCH-10 this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 insurer and the respondent No.2 RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.1 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2, has to pay the compensation of Rs.7,01,800/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,01,800/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
SCCH-10
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

The respondent No.1 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Out of the award amount, 40% of the award amount shall be invested in fixed deposit for a period of 2 years in any nationalized bank of petitioner's choice and balance Vivek Narayan Singh vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173834261/
8 amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner through NEFT / RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
